2610.13607.title: BLiMPPI: Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs for Polarity Items
2610.13607.paper_summary: Negative polarity items (NPIs), such as "anymore" and "ever", are grammatical only in select environments, predominantly in the context of negation. Because their grammaticality depends on both syntax and semantics, they have a rich, multilingual literature in theoretical linguistics, yet work on NPIs in language models is almost entirely confined to English. We introduce BLiMPPI, a multilingual evaluation suite of over 12,000 NPI minimal pairs in 33 languages, built by a pipeline that discovers NPIs in Universal Dependencies (UD) treebanks, labels their licensing environments, and perturbs these into minimal pairs. Evaluating 12 multilingual and 2 monolingual models alongside n-gram baselines, we find that multilingual models struggle most with lower-resource languages and with pairs that are not n-gram solvable. We further examine the effects of NPI typology, language family, licensing variability, and NPI-licenser distance. Data: https://github.com/arzuburcuguven/blimppi-data
2610.13607.paper_summary_zh: 負極性項目（NPI），例如「anymore」和「ever」，僅在特定環境中具有語法正確性，主要是在否定的語境中。因為它們的語法性依賴於語法和語義，因此在理論語言學中有著豐富的多語言文獻，但在語言模型中對NPI的研究幾乎完全限於英語。我們介紹BLiMPPI，一個包含33種語言中超過12,000個NPI最小對的多語言評估套件，該套件通過一個管道發現Universal Dependencies（UD）樹庫中的NPI，標記其授權環境，並將其擾動為最小對。在評估12個多語言模型和2個單語言模型以及n-gram基準時，我們發現多語言模型在低資源語言和不適合n-gram解決的對上最為困難。我們進一步檢查了NPI類型、語言家族、授權變異性和NPI-授權者距離的影響。數據：https://github.com/arzuburcuguven/blimppi-data
